claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and would like to know if I'm eligible.

I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm pleased to help you assess eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

To determine if you're eligible, I need to gather some details about your circumstances. Let me start:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand your residency status, as this is an important factor for Child Benefit eligibility.

**What is your residency status in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK - I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Now I need to understand Alex's circumstances a bit better.

**Is Alex in full-time education or approved training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in education - he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. I have one more important question:

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or have you previously received it for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently receiving it - that's why I'm inquiring now to see if I can claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me evaluate this based on the Child Benefit rules:

**Key findings:**
- Alex is 18 years old
- Alex is in full-time education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- You are a British citizen resident in the UK
- You are not currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex

Under Child Benefit rules, you can receive Child Benefit for a young person aged 16-19 if they are in approved full-time education or training. Since Alex is 18 and in full-time education at sixth form college studying for A-levels, this is an approved form of full-time education.

Your residency status as a British citizen also meets the residency requirements for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Alex qualifies because:
- He is within the eligible age range (16-19 years old)
- He is in full-time education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- You meet the residency requirements as a British citizen

You should be able to make a claim for Child Benefit. If you'd like to proceed, you can contact HMRC or apply through the appropriate channels to start your claim.
